# AngelBot release runbook

AngelBot keeps development, desktop E2E, and production update capabilities
separate. A normal local release build creates the supported per-user NSIS
installer without any updater key. The GitHub release workflow is the only path that enables the
updater plugin and creates signed update artifacts.

## Repository workflow

- `dev` is the current default/integration branch. Use short-lived
  `codex/<change>` branches and open PRs targeting `dev`; do not commit or push
  directly to it. Community contributors can use their own fork/branch names.
  `main` is reserved for stable promotions; it does not exist on the remote yet.
  Do not publish the unrelated old local `main` branch as part of this setup.
- Commit a complete, buildable change, including its frontend/backend contract,
  tests, migrations and necessary documentation. Do not split coupled changes
  merely to make commits smaller. Run `python scripts/verify.py full` before a
  checkpoint; automated verification must not need model credentials or user data.
- Use `npm ci` and `package-lock.json` for frontend dependencies, and keep
  `src-tauri/Cargo.lock` for the application. Do not introduce a second package
  manager lockfile or update dependencies as part of unrelated cleanup.
- Keep application source and the canonical planning documents tracked. Tauri's
  `src-tauri/gen/schemas/` is generated by the build and stays local, as do test
  runtime data, screenshots, credentials, signing private keys and build outputs.
- Keep source line endings governed by `.gitattributes`; avoid unrelated
  whole-tree normalization when recording a feature checkpoint.
- Rust formatting is checked through the same canonical runner (`cargo fmt
  --check`), alongside TypeScript compilation, tests and diff hygiene. Use
  `.editorconfig` and `.gitattributes` for editor/line-ending consistency. Do not
  silence warnings, weaken assertions or add a second test framework to pass CI.
- PR titles use `type(scope): summary` (scope optional): `feat`, `fix`, `docs`,
  `refactor`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `perf`, or `revert`. Mark unfinished
  changes as draft. Keep intermediate commits useful without forcing a rewrite.
- Use `.github/pull_request_template.md` to record purpose, verification,
  compatibility/recovery risks and reviewer findings. Review naming, module
  boundaries, reuse, duplication, obsolete paths and sensitive/generated files;
  tests do not replace this review. AI review is supplementary, not human approval.
- Squash short-lived feature PRs into `dev`, using the reviewed PR title as the
  final commit subject. Promote `dev` to `main` with a merge commit so ancestry
  remains intact. Keep squash and merge enabled; do not require linear history
  for the long-lived promotion branch or enable automatic merging.
- The merge checks are `Windows full verification`, `Windows desktop smoke test`
  and `PR policy`. The latter handles title edits without rerunning Windows builds.
  Setup fetches locked dependencies; test execution is offline and isolated.
  Never use `pull_request_target`, repository secrets or a self-hosted desktop
  runner to execute contributor code.
- One maintainer cannot approve their own PR: use zero mandatory approvals until
  another eligible reviewer joins, while still requiring explicit maintainer
  review/merge and resolved conversations. Do not require all-tree CODEOWNERS.
- GitHub protection/rulesets are remote settings, not enabled by these files.
  Once available, require PRs and the three checks, current base checks and resolved
  conversations; block force pushes/deletions and administrator bypass. Keep a
  single protection mechanism, and verify the actual rules after configuring it.
  The private repository returned HTTP 403 during setup; do not claim an enforced
  merge gate while that limitation remains. Reference: `PR-WORKFLOW-REFERENCE.md`.
- Local automatic post-commit pushing is disabled. The previous hook is retained
  at `.git/hooks/post-commit.autopush-disabled` for recovery, not execution. Hooks
  are local metadata: inspect existing hooks before each first commit in a checkout;
  do not install automatic pushes in clones.
- Before cleaning historical references, save and verify a local Git bundle.
  Prune only registrations whose worktree directories no longer exist, and
  delete only inactive branches already merged into the current integration
  branch. Leave existing worktrees, unmerged branches and stashes intact; their
  owning runtime must finish its own lifecycle cleanup.
- A development checkpoint is not a release. Record real-window/model and
  installer acceptance gaps in `docs/current-roadmap.md`; do not create a `v*`
  release tag or push any remote without an explicit release/push request.

### Publication boundary

The owner chose MIT and authorized public visibility after checks pass. Current
source checks did not confirm live credentials, but the existing remote `dev`
history contains deleted personal documents and browser traces. Publication is
therefore blocked until the owner chooses an explicit history cleanup strategy;
do not make the repository public or force-rewrite its history as a side effect
of setting up PRs. Keep the private history and local recovery bundle protected.

## One-time repository setup

1. Generate the updater key pair on a trusted machine:

   ```powershell
   npm run tauri -- signer generate --write-keys "$env:USERPROFILE\.tauri\angelbot-updater.key"
   ```

2. Store the private key contents in the GitHub Actions secret
   `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`.
3. If the key has a password, store it in
   `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`.
4. Store the public key contents in the GitHub repository variable
   `TAURI_UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY`.

Never commit either key or the generated `src-tauri/tauri.release.conf.json`.
The release workflow writes that config from the public key at runtime.

The updater signature proves that an update came from AngelBot. Windows
Authenticode signing is a separate distribution requirement: configure a
trusted Windows code-signing certificate before treating the installer as a
public, warning-free download.

## Release procedure

1. Update the same SemVer version in `package.json`, `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, and
   `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`.
2. Run:

   ```powershell
   python scripts/verify.py full
   npm run test:desktop
   npm run release:build
   ```

3. Smoke-test the locally produced NSIS installer in
   `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`.
4. Create and push the matching tag, for example `v0.1.0`. The release
   preflight rejects tags that do not match the application version.
5. GitHub Actions creates a draft release containing the NSIS installer, signatures,
   and `latest.json`. Install the draft artifacts on a clean Windows account
   and verify launch, first-run setup, project creation, and update behavior.
6. Publish the draft only after the smoke test passes. Draft releases are not
   served by the `releases/latest/download/latest.json` updater endpoint.

## Recovery

Do not silently downgrade an installed application. If a draft is broken,
delete or replace it before publishing. If a published build is broken, mark
it as non-latest and ship a higher patch version containing the fix. Keep the
previous installers available for manual recovery until the patch is proven.
